method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

items.assessment: Hemodynamic instability takes priority over plausible diagnostic and preparation tasks; key and rationale are defensible.
Constipation and new infectious findings are specific plausible precipitants, while chronic stable findings do not explain the change.
The infection pattern is sound, but the girth alternative advertises an unjustified tomorrow delay.
issues: The infection pattern is sound, but the girth alternative advertises an unjustified tomorrow delay.
proposedChanges: Use a plain competing assessment such as measuring current girth and weight; explain its lower priority in the rationale.

items.assessment: Post-drainage circulatory deterioration is clear, but walking and eating are weak responses to marked hypotension and dizziness.
issues: Post-drainage circulatory deterioration is clear, but walking and eating are weak responses to marked hypotension and dizziness.
proposedChanges: Use credible competing assessments such as checking the puncture site, reviewing volume removed, or repeating a manual blood pressure; retain a concise immediate safety/support response.

items.assessment: Reduced responsiveness with ongoing hematemesis makes airway protection the immediate priority even while crossmatch preparation is important.
Early feeding premise is useful, but loud bowel sounds and forcing a full meal make alternatives conspicuously weak.
issues: Early feeding premise is useful, but loud bowel sounds and forcing a full meal make alternatives conspicuously weak.
proposedChanges: Compare the ordered feeding trial with waiting for enzyme normalization, starting with a clear-liquid trial, and choosing an initial meal portion based mainly on calorie targets; explain why current tolerance cues support the order.

items.assessment: Respiratory and perfusion deterioration distinguish systemic complications from improving abdominal symptoms.
Meal-linked enzyme timing is useful; removing all fat and tracking stool colour are implausible substitutes that make the answer too easy.
issues: Meal-linked enzyme timing is useful; removing all fat and tracking stool colour are implausible substitutes that make the answer too easy.
proposedChanges: Use a lower-fat meal plan, an increased bedtime enzyme dose, and a food/stool-frequency diary as plausible competing responses. Explain why meal timing addresses the presented error.

items.assessment: Observed external compression supports correcting the mechanical problem before changing suction, tube position, or symptom treatment.
The bowel ischemia/perforation warning pattern is sound, but walking, oral fluid, and waiting until the next round are weak alternatives.
issues: The bowel ischemia/perforation warning pattern is sound, but walking, oral fluid, and waiting until the next round are weak alternatives.
proposedChanges: Consider parallel interpretations of the changed pain pattern, or credible competing assessments/ordered symptom treatment without delay clauses.

items.assessment: The change from usual diarrhea to vomiting, distension, and absent stool/flatus supports a possible obstructive complication; parallel interpretations are credible.
Fewer stools can coexist with worsening systemic and abdominal signs; the keyed combination addresses a meaningful deterioration trap.
Dusky cool stoma supports urgent perfusion review, but wait/routine modifiers advertise the wrong choices.
issues: Dusky cool stoma supports urgent perfusion review, but wait/routine modifiers advertise the wrong choices.
proposedChanges: Present the competing actions directly: warm local compress, adjust the barrier opening, or record stoma appearance; keep rationale focused on the perfusion change rather than artificial delay.

items.assessment: Urine decline and orthostatic symptoms are relevant systemic evidence of high-output fluid loss; local healthy findings do not exclude dehydration.
The obstruction concern is defensible, but a bulky meal to push contents and irrigation with pouch-cleaning equipment are cartoon unsafe alternatives.
issues: The obstruction concern is defensible, but a bulky meal to push contents and irrigation with pouch-cleaning equipment are cartoon unsafe alternatives.
proposedChanges: Replace those choices with clinically credible responses a learner might prioritize, such as checking barrier fit or applying the existing hydration plan, and keep the urgent assessment keyed to the combined absent output, pain, distension, and nausea.

items.assessment: New dysphagia and weight loss are useful alarm features; month/year delays make alternatives easy to reject on wording.
issues: New dysphagia and weight loss are useful alarm features; month/year delays make alternatives easy to reject on wording.
proposedChanges: Remove the arbitrary delays and compare prompt review with the stated food-trigger, bite-size, and meal-timing strategies as plain actions.

items.assessment: Inability to manage saliva with preserved breathing distinguishes urgent esophageal impaction from complete airway obstruction; the fluid/food attempts are recognizable misconceptions.
Timing after a sugary drink supports early dumping; the meal/fluids plan competes with plausible but counterproductive calorie or hypoglycemia responses.
The combined postoperative pain, fever, tachycardia, and drainage change supports escalation over plausible isolated symptom measures.
Persistent shock despite absent visible bleeding repeats the same objective as adaptation026/027 and the acute GI-bleed item101.
issues: Persistent shock despite absent visible bleeding repeats the same objective as adaptation026/027 and the acute GI-bleed item101.
proposedChanges: Replace with the proposed distinct late-dumping scenario, with explicit postprandial timing and glucose data, and a task that distinguishes late from early dumping or evaluates a prevention plan.

items.assessment: Biliary infection with shock is clinically compelling, but meal and warm-comfort options are weak against hypotension, fever, and jaundice.
issues: Biliary infection with shock is clinically compelling, but meal and warm-comfort options are weak against hypotension, fever, and jaundice.
proposedChanges: Use parallel clinical concerns or relevant competing assessment actions; distinguish complicated biliary infection from biliary colic, pancreatitis, and uncomplicated hepatitis without artificially delayed choices.

items.assessment: A sudden generalized rigid abdomen changes the priority from usual ulcer symptom treatment to urgent suspected perforation care.
Tachycardia and new pain/restlessness after bariatric surgery warrant assessment despite no fever; gas pain and analgesia responses represent plausible anchoring errors.
Normal mucus secretion from retained bowel is useful teaching; appliance leakage internally is an implausible anatomical mechanism.
issues: Normal mucus secretion from retained bowel is useful teaching; appliance leakage internally is an implausible anatomical mechanism.
proposedChanges: Replace that distractor with a credible interpretation such as clearance of residual distal stool, and make the clear mucus description/time context sufficient to distinguish it.

items.assessment: Improvement in attention, orientation, and command-following is more directly relevant than sedation-related quietness or bilirubin trend.
